put.description:
Change selected settings on an account-owned agent. Although the method is PUT, this is a partial update: omitted fields keep their saved values. Creation defaults are not reapplied. Send JSON booleans and numbers, not strings. A null value is allowed only where stated. Changing voice_key, voice_id or language revalidates the resulting voice selection; use one identifier or a matching pair. A language-only update rechecks the existing voice. Enabling voicemail is checked against the merged saved/request state. Unknown fields are ignored only alongside a supported field and appear in warnings.

The system_prompt limit is 3,000 tokens with knowledge enabled, otherwise 16,000 characters. A 100,000-character parsing ceiling is not the accepted prompt size. Extraction definitions reject unknown nested fields and reserve __proto__, constructor and prototype. Compatibility fields remain stored settings and do not necessarily select runtime behaviour.

Customer keyterms: at most 20 nonempty comma-separated terms, at most 50 Unicode characters per trimmed term, and a conservative 450-byte total safety budget for changed values. The text field also has a 2,000-character ceiling. Empty entries do not count; repeated nonempty terms count separately toward 20. Null clears the list. On update, omitted values are retained. An exact unchanged saved string is kept even if it exceeds the newer count, term-length, size or text limits. Any change must meet all current limits.

The safety byte count normalizes each trimmed term (NFKD, removes combining marks, lowercases, removes whitespace) to detect duplicates. Each unique normalized term costs the UTF-8 bytes of its first trimmed original spelling plus 4 bytes. Empty and duplicate normalized terms add no bytes. This conservative count is not a tokenizer. Term length counts Unicode code points, not UTF-16 code units.

Automatic knowledge terms are read-only. They come from valid, unsuppressed live pieces, keep source spelling, and are ranked by importance, essential identity, repeated support and stable tie-breaks. Generic terms are filtered. The default limit is 80 per agent; platform configuration can choose 0–100. Customer terms take priority and stay first on calls; duplicates and weaker automatic terms are removed to fit the call limits. The returned list is not a promise that every term will be sent on a call. Read [automatic keyterms](/api-reference/knowledge/get-agents-target-knowledge-keyterms).

More than 20 changed terms returns 400 invalid_agent_field with message "Keep up to 20 words - remove some to save" and details.field "boosted_keywords". The count check runs before term-length and safety-byte checks. DELETE switches is_active to false; it does not remove the record. GET by owned agent ID still returns the inactive agent. The default active-only list omits it; status=disabled or status=all includes it.

get.description: Read a filtered call-history envelope with matching totals. History includes failed starts and omits transcripts, event data, extracted data and recording URLs. Order is created_at descending, nulls last, then row ID descending. The cursor binds the account, filters and first-page time boundary. Send only cursor and optional limit for the next page. Stop when has_more is false and next_cursor is null; stop on a repeated cursor. This is not a frozen database snapshot: later updates and deletion can change results. The default period is the preceding 30 days. Cost sums include only known values; cost_unknown counts rows excluded from that sum. Null success is not a failed call. outcome=failed selects failed starts; their IDs can begin failed:. A retained call_summary can still be present, so treat the result as private account data. For recording availability and temporary download access, use [Get a call recording](/api-reference/calls/get-calls-id-recording).

post.description:
Start one outbound call from an account-owned number assigned to an active agent. A 201 response means the call was initiated; it does not prove connection, conversation, completion or a successful outcome. Only send to a recipient you are authorised to contact. This endpoint has no dry-run option. The examples use an explicit recipient variable and can place a real call when run. Optional recipient location values do not override suppression, contact hours or capacity rules.

Use dynamic_vars for single-call substitutions; campaign recipient variables are a different contract. There is no fallback to an agent-level phone_number. When from_number is omitted, selection uses the oldest eligible number by creation time then row ID. Selection does not bypass the final ownership and availability checks. Contact-hours refusals use error.code outside_hours or needs_timezone (409), or contact_policy_unavailable (503). Details include outcome:not_sent, sent:false and charged:false. Advisory messages can instead start “Outside calling hours” or “Weekend where they are” and contain the next local window. single_contact_policy is an internal policy-check name, not an HTTP error code. refused_before_dispatch is a dispatch outcome marker, not an HTTP status or a replacement error.code. Unknown outcome is not proof that nothing was sent.

patch.description: Change per-number settings, or move the number to another active agent on the same account. A move and a settings update are separate requests. Omitted settings remain unchanged. The six strict switches below accept only JSON booleans; sms_reply_enabled and older override fields retain their documented legacy coercion. Use canonical snake_case names. A saved web_calls_enabled value is not proof that all effective web-call prerequisites are satisfied. ### Number controls The seven switches cover inbound, outbound, SMS reply, web agent, web calls, web functions and saved monitor permission. Off switches can prevent new work without ending an existing call. Read the number to confirm saved and effective state. ### Move to another agent Send only `{ "agent_id": "agent_TARGET" }`. The move preserves number-specific settings and history and does not change carrier routing. New work uses the target agent. A busy number is refused. Repeating the same settled assignment returns changed: false. The move response contains agent_name and changed, while a settings response contains saved settings. Read web_calls_effective from the number detail endpoint to check effective website access. Saved permission does not start a monitor session. Never delete and re-import a number just to move it between agents.

post.description:
Send one SMS using an explicit sender owned by the account and assigned to the requested agent. A 201 sent response means the send was accepted; it is not proof of delivery to the recipient. The endpoint has no dry-run mode. Only send to an authorised recipient. Do not infer a sender from agent settings, and do not send API credentials to a browser. The response can gain receipt fields when that feature is enabled; older successful responses contain only status, to and from.

An accepted message can still return 201 if later local history persistence fails. A receipt-path failure can include outcome, work_id, message_id and safe_to_retry both alongside the error and inside details. Do not infer not-sent from a generic 500 response. Contact-hours refusals use error.code outside_hours or needs_timezone (409), or contact_policy_unavailable (503). Details include outcome:not_sent, sent:false and charged:false. Advisory messages can instead start “Outside calling hours” or “Weekend where they are” and contain the next local window. single_contact_policy is an internal policy-check name, not an HTTP error code. refused_before_dispatch is a dispatch outcome marker, not an HTTP status or a replacement error.code. Unknown outcome is not proof that nothing was sent.

Create a voice campaign and its recipient rows. The default now mode immediately requests launch; schedule mode saves scheduled work that can run automatically. There is no public draft-only flag. ### Scheduling, consent and duplicate rows

The scheduler and final contact checks use recipient-local eligibility, consent, suppression and capacity. A campaign time zone is not a substitute for an unknown recipient location. Preview contact hours before saving; a preview is advisory. Wider hours require the recorded explanation and remain subject to policy.

Choose duplicate_policy deliberately. reject refuses repeated accepted numbers, allow keeps every row, and warn reports duplicates but still allows this route to request launch. The duplicate_choice_required response flag is advisory. It does not create a safe draft or block sending.

The scheduled example can contact its recipients when due. Use an approved destination and consent; the date is illustrative. No public draft-only flag is accepted. No public voice campaign delete route is available. Reuse replaces the recipient list and settings only while the owned campaign has never launched.

JSON request size and database constraints can limit a request before the maximum accepted-recipient count. No additional text length limit is declared for the prompt or message template on this route.

post.description:
Create an SMS campaign and its recipient rows. The default now mode immediately requests launch; schedule mode saves scheduled work that can run automatically. There is no public draft-only flag. ### Scheduling, consent and duplicate rows

The scheduler and final contact checks use recipient-local eligibility, consent, suppression and capacity. A campaign time zone is not a substitute for an unknown recipient location. Preview contact hours before saving; a preview is advisory. Wider hours require the recorded explanation and remain subject to policy.

Choose duplicate_policy deliberately. reject refuses repeated accepted numbers, allow keeps every row, and warn reports duplicates but still allows this route to request launch. The duplicate_choice_required response flag is advisory. It does not create a safe draft or block sending.

The scheduled example can contact its recipients when due. Use an approved destination and consent; the date is illustrative. No public draft-only flag is accepted. SMS creation always creates a new campaign. reuse_campaign_id does not implement SMS reuse; do not send it.

JSON request size and database constraints can limit a request before the maximum accepted-recipient count. No additional text length limit is declared for the prompt or message template on this route.

Read one owned SMS campaign with recipient and message history. The campaign counters cover the whole campaign; the two history lists have independent cursors. Provide limit to request bounded pages. Each list is ordered by id ascending and advances independently. Keep an exhausted list finished in your client; omitting its cursor restarts that list. This compatibility mode is not a snapshot. Invalid limits or malformed UUID cursors currently return 500 server_error; a missing campaign or failed initial lookup returns 404 not_found. Retention can remove content between reads.

put.description: Save Cal.com settings for an owned phone number. This replaces the saved configuration for this integration; omitted configuration values do not preserve the old values. Per-number calendar settings override agent settings. A conflict with another booking calendar is checked only after number ownership. This endpoint does not connect or disconnect other integrations. Google Calendar connects through the dashboard authorisation flow; no public API-key connection endpoint is provided. HTTP 409 booking_provider_conflict refuses a competing calendar before saving. The error identifies the connected provider in details.connected_provider. Number connections and the agent-level fallback are both checked; changing is_active does not bypass that guard. Number-level message pattern: `CALENDAR is already connected to NUMBER. Only one booking calendar can be connected to a number at a time - the AI would be given both sets of booking tools and would silently use only one. Disconnect CALENDAR first, then connect Cal.com.` Agent-level message pattern: `CALENDAR is already connected to this agent, which covers every number on it. Only one booking calendar can be active at a time. Disconnect CALENDAR first, then connect Cal.com.` CALENDAR and NUMBER are replaced with the connected calendar label and owned number.

Preview source token usage before an import without storing the source. This authenticated POST is a read-only calculation and needs no Idempotency-Key. It does not reserve capacity, call a paid model or save a file/base. Import checks totals again.

Raw upload: Content-Type application/octet-stream, X-Filename, optional X-Source-Title and X-Review; replacements also require X-Expected-Revision. File maximum 10 MiB; PDF maximum 200 pages. Accept clean UTF-8 text, PDF with selectable text, or DOCX. No raw base64/path input, RTF, executable or active-content documents. Preview scan status is not publication clearance. Without a configured scanner, local_checks_only permits bounded local checks. With a configured scanner, PDF/DOCX need a clean result; clean UTF-8 text can use local checks during an outage. Infected files never bypass. Imports may wait at safety_check/safety_waiting with next_retry_at; after 24 hours scan_expired requires a new upload. Raw files are private and never downloaded; accepted storage retains extracted text.

Agent list/detail reads also expose knowledge_keyterms when knowledge is enabled and filter against saved customer words.
